scope: Development integration of bounded raw ownership reconstruction with the final resource adapter, retained-file loader and regression policy. No final performance campaign is admitted.
changes: CPU comparisons use originalOwnerInclusiveCpuSeconds from the original terminal wait4 receipt exactly once; sampledProcessCpuSeconds remains explicitly named legacy diagnostics.
The loader validates raw inventory shapes, counts and byte totals before member reads, then enforces actual member size before allocation and reconstructs original custody internally.
Controlled component attribution comes from reconstructed roles, including the reference worker hosting its driver code; metadata labels cannot add application/database/mail owners.
Raw callback identity, worker, dispatch interval, outcome and original runner exit join the normalized report. The runner terminal observations also join the owner report.

Capture metadata joins declared host/boot, source/dependency and executable identities; resource collector admission is scoped to that complete context. Context consistency is not independent authenticity proof.
Acquisition-boundary RSS remains included. Unsampled owned nodes retain terminal CPU coverage without invented RSS observations.

verification.review: Read-only independent review identified missing raw outcome/runner-exit joins and collector-admission context binding. Both were corrected with regression controls. Final review found no remaining blocking integration defect.
earlierAttemptsRetained: Initial Bun invocation omitted explicit relative file prefixes and found no tests.
Initial integration run passed 180 tests and failed two outdated rejection-message/fixture expectations; corrected controls precede final 227-test verification.

rawReplay.bindingMode: Retrospective synthetic context labels solely to exercise projection. No original host/boot/source/executable admission is claimed.

limits.scope: Byte budgets include raw JSONL retained reads. Parsed object overhead and process RSS are not bounded by these byte limits.

limitations: Real normalized fixtures and retained captures verify reconstruction; their adapter context metadata is explicitly synthetic/retrospective and cannot supply prospective host/boot/source/executable admission.
Only the six controlled-family schemas are implemented; application/external backend ownership remains outside this adapter.
Current source/workload/instrumentation admission and a fresh prospective complete campaign remain required.
Legacy sampled-diagnostic conversion is retained for diagnostic regressions and synthetic policy controls; its schema 1 output is rejected by final CPU admission.
No Rust/browser/runtime behavior was changed. Focused development checks do not replace a current full core, release package or native Linux gate.
